title: Impact of Irrigation Eligibility on Crop Revenue

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is appropriate here because treatment (irrigation eligibility) is determined by a sharp cutoff rule based on land slope. The key assumption is that farmers cannot precisely manipulate their land slope around the threshold, ensuring quasi-random assignment of treatment status near the cutoff. This allows us to identify the local average treatment effect of irrigation eligibility on crop revenue.

## 2. R Code
```r
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s96_data.csv")

# Determine the cutoff point by examining where treatment changes
cutoff <- max(data$running_var[data$treated == 0])
cat("Cutoff point:", cutoff, "\n")

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$running_var, 
                      c = cutoff,
                      kernel = "triangular",
                      bwselect = "mserd")

# Print main results
cat("\n=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Local Average Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Bandwidth:", round(rdd_result$bws[1], 4), "\n")
cat("N Left of cutoff:", rdd_result$N[1], ", N Right of cutoff:", rdd_result$N[2], "\n")

# Robustness check 1: Alternative bandwidth
rdd_robust1 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var, 
                       c = cutoff,
                       h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 0.75)

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: 75% Bandwidth ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_robust1$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_robust1$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Robustness check 2: Different kernel
rdd_robust2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var, 
                       c = cutoff,
                       kernel = "uniform")

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: Uniform Kernel ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_robust2$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_robust2$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Placebo test: Test for discontinuity at false cutoff
false_cutoff <- cutoff - 0.1
rdd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var, 
                       c = false_cutoff)

cat("\n=== PLACEBO TEST: False Cutoff ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect at false cutoff:", round(rdd_placebo$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_placebo$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Visualization
plot_data <- data
plot_data$distance_from_cutoff <- plot_data$running_var - cutoff

# Create RDD plot
p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = distance_from_cutoff, y = y)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(treated)), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(plot_data, distance_from_cutoff < 0), 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(plot_data, distance_from_cutoff >= 0), 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Impact of Irrigation Eligibility on Crop Revenue",
       x = "Land Slope (Centered at Cutoff)",
       y = "Crop Revenue",
       color = "Irrigation Eligible") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("The local average treatment effect of irrigation eligibility is:", 
    round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
if(rdd_result$pv[1] < 0.05) {
  cat("This effect is statistically significant at the 5% level.\n")
} else {
  cat("This effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and significant treatment effect, with irrigation eligibility increasing crop revenue by approximately 0.15-0.25 units. This is because irrigation typically improves crop yields by providing consistent water supply, especially during dry periods. The magnitude should be economically meaningful since access to irrigation is a fundamental agricultural input that directly affects productivity and farmer income. The effect should be most pronounced for farms just above the slope threshold where the quasi-experimental variation is strongest.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare crop revenue for farms just above and below the slope threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for irrigation increases crop revenue.
